Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: Ministry of Health with WHO/UNICEF support uses digital health information systems (DHIS2) for disease surveillance and supply chains nationwide. These function as parallel donor-driven infrastructure, not integrated into a national government data exchange.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original single source confirmed but Value Code recalculated. A 2024/25 Health Information System maturity assessment rates 'systems for data and information communication and use' at only 37% ('Minimal Maturity', overall HIS maturity 40.5%), and DHIS2 remains a donor-run parallel platform (Ministry of Health/WHO/UNICEF) with no documented plan to feed data into a cross-government data exchange. No source found evidencing an actual integration plan, so downgraded from 'Planned' (2) to 'Not integrated' (1).

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: Digital border management systems emerging at Nimule one-stop border post. Customs automation and electronic clearance under development. Not yet integrated into a national data exchange platform.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Fresher reporting (Jan 2026-July 2026) shows the Civil Registry/Passport/Immigration Directorate has digitised its own payment link and is progressively connecting embassies to a central online passport system, but Sudans Post (19 Jan 2026) explicitly states South Sudan 'still lacks a national digital identity system' and that immigration data operates as an isolated project without interoperability across civil registry, banking or other government systems. No plan for integration into a cross-government data exchange is documented, so downgraded from 'Planned' (2) to 'Not integrated' (1); the Nimule OSBP project (EU/UNOPS/TradeMark Africa, launched Sept 2025) is a border-facility consolidation project, not evidence of data-exchange integration.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: Inter-Bank Payment and Settlement System launched Oct 2025 by Bank of South Sudan enables interoperable payments between commercial banks. G2P payment integration exists for some government salary payments but is not linked to a broader data exchange platform.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Bank of South Sudan's Inter-Bank Payment and Settlement System (SSIPSS), launched 10 October 2025 with 13 commercial banks connected by November 2025 (mandatory compliance deadline 31 Jan 2026), is explicitly described by officials as 'laying the foundation for interoperable digital public infrastructure' and expected to support future digitisation of government payments and e-government platforms, but G2P/G2B integration via a data exchange has not yet materialised. 'Planned' (2) is confirmed with fresher, corroborating sources.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Updated to fresher evidence (Sept 2025): the South Sudan Revenue Authority's eTax and eCustoms platforms remain separate systems; a Sept 2025 SSRA management review flagged only the need for stronger integration between these two internal platforms, not evidence of any plan to link tax/revenue data into a wider cross-government data exchange. Downgraded from 'Planned' (2) to 'Not integrated' (1) and year updated from 2022 to 2025 to reflect the newer source.
